title: Bakery and Garden
premise: Odile Dravenmoor inherited her grandmother's failing vineyard along with crushing debts, and she has trained herself to feel nothing that can't be budgeted. When her family reunion threatens to expose how far she's fallen, she hires Theo Marchetti, a baker who rents her crumbling garden cottage, to pose as her partner for one weekend. The fake date curdles into something real by dessert, but Odile's creditors are closing in on the vineyard, and the only escape is selling to a developer who will raze Theo's bakery block. To save both the land and the man she's come to love, Odile must forgive herself for the choices survival forced on her — and in the final chapter, she signs the vineyard over to a worker cooperative co-founded with Theo, choosing belonging over ownership.
about_author: Edmund Ishikawa is the pen name of a former sommelier who spent a decade working harvest seasons across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes romances about people who mistake self-sufficiency for safety, and he still bakes sourdough every Sunday.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Hearts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She audits the vineyard's debts at her kitchen table and rehearses the lie she'll tell at the family reunion: that her life is thriving. A letter from the bank gives her ninety days. The emotional beat is controlled dread masked as competence.

chapters.title: Bread and Borrowed Light
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He opens his bakery before dawn in the shadow of the development notice taped to his door. When Odile arrives to collect back rent from her cottage tenant — herself being his landlord — their transactional relationship crackles with mutual wariness. Beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: A Proposal Over Proofing Dough
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Desperate after her sister calls to confirm plus-ones, Odile offers Theo free rent for a year if he plays her boyfriend for the reunion weekend. He refuses twice, then sees the developer's name on her creditor list. Beat: a bargain struck with unspoken stakes.

chapters.title: Rehearsal in the Vine Rows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They practice their story among the dying vines — how they met, first kiss, inside jokes. The rehearsal keeps dissolving into real conversation about grief: his late mother, her grandmother. Beat: intimacy arriving through fiction's back door.

chapters.title: The Dravenmoor Reunion
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Arrival at her aunt's estate; her sister Vivienne clocks the lie immediately but says nothing in front of the cousins. Theo performs flawlessly, too flawlessly, charming even Odile's cruelest uncle. Beat: the thrill of being believed.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. During dessert, Odile's hand finds his under the table without prompting. Later, on the terrace, she almost tells him the truth about the debts and stops. They share a kiss that neither planned. Beat: the fake date tipping past its borders.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Minus Seven
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Back home, she throws herself into vineyard repairs while avoiding Theo. Her accountant delivers worse news: the developer's offer is now the only viable exit, and it requires evicting the bakery tenants. Beat: guilt calcifying into secrecy.

chapters.title: What the Garden Knows
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He tends Odile's neglected garden uninvited, finding her grandmother's journals buried in the potting shed — records of every harvest, every debt forgiven between neighbors. Beat: Theo begins understanding the woman behind the ledger.

chapters.title: Sunday Customers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She visits the bakery openly for the first time and is absorbed into its orbit of regulars — the widow who orders rye, the kids who trade chores for croissants. For an hour she belongs somewhere. Beat: found family glimpsed, then fled from.

chapters.title: Vivienne's Terms
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her sister confronts her privately: she knows about the money, knows about the fake boyfriend, and offers to buy the vineyard herself — if Odile admits publicly that she failed. Beat: pride versus rescue, and the mirror held up.

chapters.title: The Second Weekend
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A cousin's engagement party demands a return appearance. This time nothing is performed; they dance like people who mean it, and afterward Theo asks what happens when the contract ends. Odile changes the subject. Beat: desire outrunning denial.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She signs a preliminary agreement with the developer, hiding it in the same drawer as her grandmother's journals. That night Theo finds the papers while returning a borrowed ladder. Beat: the secret surfaces, and silence becomes betrayal.

chapters.title: Sourdough and Silence
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Wounded, Theo doesn't confront her — he withdraws, canceling their next 'date.' The bakery regulars notice his flat loaves. Odile notices the empty garden. Beat: the cost of survival priced in loneliness.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Margins
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reading the journals fully, she discovers her grandmother nearly lost the vineyard twice and was saved twice by neighbors — including Theo's grandfather, whose bakery once fed the harvest crews on credit. Beat: history insisting on interdependence.

chapters.title: The Apology That Isn't Enough
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She goes to Theo and confesses everything: the debts, the sale, the shame. He listens, then says forgiveness isn't his to give — she has to stop punishing herself first. Beat: truth spoken, reconciliation deferred.

chapters.title: Cooperative Dreams
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inspired by the journals, Theo proposes an alternative: convert the vineyard and bakery block into a cooperative, with tenants and workers buying shares. It's audacious, probably impossible, and the first plan that saves everyone. Beat: hope with a business model.

chapters.title: Racing the Foreclosure
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sixty hours remain before the developer's contract locks. Odile works the phones — Vivienne, the credit union, the tenants — while Theo rallies the neighborhood. Every door half-opens. Beat: rising tension, the clock audible in every scene.

chapters.title: The Family Vote
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At an emergency family gathering, Odile stands before the Dravenmoors and admits her failure aloud — no performance, no plus-one. Vivienne, moved, pledges her own savings instead of buying control. Beat: the person in the mirror finally forgiven.

chapters.title: Signatures
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Climax. In the bakery, surrounded by flour-dusted witnesses, the cooperative papers are signed as the developer's lawyer waits futilely at the vineyard gate. The last signature needed is Odile's — and she hesitates, then signs not as owner but as member. Beat: triumph earned collectively.

chapters.title: First Harvest Together
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Weeks later, the whole improbable family harvests the vines — cousins, bakers, widows, children. Odile and Theo steal a moment between rows where their first rehearsal kiss happened. Beat: abundance replacing austerity.

chapters.title: The Heart, Retrained
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Quiet epilogue-adjacent chapter: Odile writes her own entry in her grandmother's journal, recording debts forgiven — starting with her own. She and Theo have their first real date, no contract attached. Beat: tenderness without terms.

chapters.title: Bakery and Garden
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, brief sections. One year on: the cooperative thrives, the garden blooms, and on a Sunday morning Theo proposes with a ring baked into a loaf — which Odile almost doesn't find. Laughter, tears, yes. Final beat: belonging chosen daily, not inherited or bought.
